{{legend0|#D3D3D3|No election}} | legend = }} The '''2022 United States elections''' are an ongoing set of elections that are primarily (with the exception of [[Absentee balloting|absentee balloting]]) held on November 8, 2022 (''[[Election Day (United States)|Election Day]]''). During this [[United States midterm election|midterm election]] year, all 435 seats in the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] and 35 of the 100 seats in the [[United States Senate|Senate]] will be contested. Thirty-nine state and territorial [[Governor#United States|gubernatorial]] elections, as well as numerous other state and local elections, will be contested. The results will determine the [[118th United States Congress]]. This will be the first election affected by the [[2022 United States redistricting|redistricting]] that followed the [[2020 United States census|2020 census]]. ==Campaign== ===Primaries=== In June 2022, ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported that Democratic campaign arms were aiding [[Far-right politics#United States|far-right]] candidates in [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[primary election|primaries]], believing they would be easier opponents in the general election.{{Cite news|newspaper=The New York Times|date=June 16, 2022|last=Weisman|first=Jonathan|title=Democrats’ Risky Bet: Aid G.O.P. Extremists in Spring, Hoping to Beat Them in Fall|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220905075301/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/06/16/us/politics/democrats-midterms-trump-gop.html|archive-date=September 5, 2022|url-access=registration|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/06/16/us/politics/democrats-midterms-trump-gop.html}} Republican primary candidates who had been endorsed by former president [[Donald Trump]] tended to win with his support being crucial for many.{{Cite news |last=Le Bars |first=Stéphanie |date=August 14, 2022 |title=Trump still has a tight grip on the Republican primaries |newspaper=Le Monde |url=https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2022/08/14/in-the-united-states-trump-s-grip-on-the-republican-primaries_5993578_4.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220906061331/https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2022/08/14/in-the-united-states-trump-s-grip-on-the-republican-primaries_5993578_4.html |archive-date=September 6, 2022}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/08/16/us/politics/trump-endorse-primary-candidates.html|url-access=registration|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903042441/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/08/16/us/politics/trump-endorse-primary-candidates.html|archive-date=September 3, 2022|title=Here’s where Trump’s endorsement record stands in Republican primaries.|last1=Astor|first1=Maggie|last2=Paybarah|first2=Azi|newspaper=The New York Times|date=August 16, 2022}} [[Progressivism in the United States#In the 21st century|Progressives]] within the Democratic Party saw mixed results, with both progressives and centrists winning important races.{{Cite news|newspaper=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/aug/06/progressives-democratic-primaries-cori-bush-rashida-tlaib|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220818135233/https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/aug/06/progressives-democratic-primaries-cori-bush-rashida-tlaib|archive-date=August 18, 2022|date=August 6, 2022|last=Greve|first=Joan E|title=Progressives bullish despite mixed results in Democratic primaries}} ===Issues=== ====Economy==== {{See also|2021–2022 inflation surge}} Voters have suffered from historically high consumer prices, gas prices, and interest rates, which Republicans have claimed have been fully or partially caused by Joe Biden's and Democratic governmental policy. The economy has been commonly cited as the top issue for voters throughout 2022.{{Cite web |last=Inc |first=Gallup |date=2022-10-31 |title=Economy Is Top Election Issue; Abortion and Crime Next |url=https://news.gallup.com/poll/404243/economy-top-election-issue-abortion-crime-next.aspx |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=Gallup.com |language=en}}{{Cite news |last=Hunnicutt |first=Trevor |last2=Bose |first2=Nandita |last3=Mason |first3=Jeff |date=2022-10-25 |title=Midterm elections outlook darkens for Biden's White House |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/midterm-elections-outlook-darkens-bidens-white-house-2022-10-25/ |access-date=2022-11-01}} ====Abortion==== {{See also|#Referendums|2022 Kansas Value Them Both Amendment|2022 California Proposition 1|2022 Michigan Proposal 3}}{{Further information|United States abortion-rights movement}} Following the [[Supreme Court of the United States|Supreme Court's]] ruling in ''[[Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization]]'' which overturned ''[[Roe v. Wade]]'' in June, Democrats outperformed [[2020 United States presidential election#Results|Biden's 2020 results]] in several House special elections, with abortion cited as a major contributor to their victories.{{Cite web |last=Reuters |date=2022-08-24 |title=Democrat who campaigned on abortion rights wins in New York special election |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/aug/24/democrat-who-campaigned-on-abortion-rights-wins-in-new-york-special-election |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=the Guardian |language=en}} The ruling has made [[abortion in the United States|abortion]] more important for voters, with a rise in support among women for the Democratic Party coming after the decision.{{Cite news|date=August 24, 2022|last=Gambino|first=Lauren|newspaper=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/aug/24/democrats-midterms-abortion-pat-ryan|title=Democrats’ hopes rise for midterms amid backlash over abortion access|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220904171459/https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/aug/24/democrats-midterms-abortion-pat-ryan|archive-date=September 4, 2022}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2022/09/05/abortion-roe-midterms/|newspaper=The Washington Post|date=September 5, 2022|last1=Knowles|first1=Hannah|last2=Kitchener|first2=Caroline|title=In sprint to November, Democrats seize on shifting landscape over abortion|url-access=subscription|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220905105459/https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2022/09/05/abortion-roe-midterms/|archive-date=September 5, 2022}} At least six states have an abortion-related ballot initiative, the most ever in a single year. ====Crime and gun violence==== [[List of mass shootings in the United States in 2022|Recent mass shootings]] have made [[Gun violence in the United States|gun violence]] and crime more important issues for voters.{{Cite web |last=Inc |first=Gallup |date=2022-10-28 |title=Record-High 56% in U.S. Perceive Local Crime Has Increased |url=https://news.gallup.com/poll/404048/record-high-perceive-local-crime-increased.aspx |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=Gallup.com |language=en}} The [[Bipartisan Safer Communities Act]], which passed in June 2022, provided extended gun-safety laws and has been touted by Biden and Democrats.{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/oct/01/gun-control-support-republicans-safer-communities-act|date=October 1, 2022|title=Gun reformers feel history is on their side despite bleak outlook in Congress|last=Greeve|first=Joan|access-date=October 26, 2022}} Despite this, Republicans have maintained a lead among voters who cite crime as a major issue.{{Cite web |last=News |first=A. B. C. |title=Crime remains top of mind for midterm voters: As Republicans pounce, Democratic leads shrink |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/crime-remains-top-mind-midterm-voters-republicans-pounce/story?id=91257218 |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=ABC News |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=In key battlegrounds, GOP onslaught of crime ads tightens Senate races |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2022-election/key-battlegrounds-gop-onslaught-crime-ads-tightens-senate-races-rcna50733 |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=NBC News |language=en}} Republicans have blamed the increase in violent crime and homicides in 2020 and 2021 on progressives and liberals, although Biden had previously rejected calls to "[[defund the police]]", a slogan supported by racial justice protesters.{{Cite web |last=Harb |first=Ali |date=2022-10-31 |title=US midterm elections: What are the key issues? |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2022/10/31/us-midterm-elections-what-are-the-key-issues-2 |access-date=2022-11-03 |website=[[Al Jazeera]] |language=en}} Democrats have pushed for stricter gun laws, including a ban on [[Assault weapon|assault weapons]], while Republicans have sought to protect access to guns and the [[Second Amendment to the United States Constitution|Second Amendment]]. ==== Democracy ==== Democrats have argued that [[Trumpism|Donald Trump supporters]] have grown increasingly [[Authoritarianism|authoritarian]] or "semi-[[Fascism|fascist]]" as Biden has called them, since Trump has continued to contest the results of the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 U.S. presidential election]]. Democrats have also argued that the Republicans regaining power would harm American governance, since the GOP has nominated many election deniers across the country for the 2022 elections. In many different states{{Citation needed|reason=Which states?|date=November 2022}}, the Democratic Party filed numerous lawsuits to remove [[Green Party (United States)|Green Party]] candidates from the ballot; most notably [[North Carolina Green Party]] Senate candidate [[2022 United States Senate election in North Carolina|Matthew Hoh.]]{{Cite web |date=2022-08-08 |title=NC Green Party claims vindication after US judge orders state to make room for party on ballot |url=https://www.wunc.org/politics/2022-08-08/nc-green-party-claims-vindication-after-federal-judge-orders-nc-to-make-room-for-greens-on-ballot |access-date=2022-11-05 |website=WUNC |language=en}} ==== Education ==== Republicans have argued for parents having more control over what their children are taught in schools, being concerned in particular with [[Race and ethnicity in the United States|race]], [[gender identity]] and [[Human sexuality|sexuality]] being discussed. Democrats have dismissed these concerns as a push for censorship, saying that it will harm LGBT students in particular. House Minority Leader [[Kevin McCarthy (California politician)|Kevin McCarthy]] has vowed to "recover lost learning from [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on education|school closures]]" during the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]. ==== Climate change ==== Progressive Democrats have pushed for legislation to combat the negative effects of [[climate change]], including incentives towards the adoption of [[renewable energy]] and [[Electric car|electric cars]]. ====Immigration==== {{See also|Immigration policy of the Joe Biden administration}} An increase of over 385% in border encounters from 2020 to 2022 has given Republicans an edge over Democrats as polling tends to show voters moderately prefer Republicans over Democrats for solving immigration problems.{{Cite web |date=September 14, 2022 |title=Nationwide Encounters |url=https://www.cbp.gov/newsroom/stats/nationwide-encounters |publisher=U.S. Customs and Border Protection}}{{Cite web | url=https://www.reuters.com/world/us/republicans-have-edge-crime-immigration-ahead-us-midterms-reutersipsos-2022-10-05 |title=Republicans have edge on crime, immigration ahead of U.S. midterms -Reuters/Ipsos poll |publisher=Reuters |date=October 5, 2022}}{{Cite web |title=Poll finds broad support in battleground states for legalizing unauthorized immigrants |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/immigration-midterms-legalization-citizenship-poll/ |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=www.cbsnews.com |language=en-US|author=Montoya-Galvez, Camilo|date=October 31, 2022}} In a political stunt, [[Ron DeSantis]] [[Martha's Vineyard migrant crisis|had migrants sent to]] [[Martha's Vineyard]]. ====Student loan forgiveness==== Since Biden revealed a plan for [[student loans in the United States|student loan]] forgiveness, both parties seek electoral gains from the decision with Republicans targeting [[Blue-collar worker|blue-collar workers]] and Democrats potentially attracting young voters.{{Cite news |last=Collinson |first=Stephen |date=August 25, 2022 |title=Biden's student loan plan opens a fresh midterm front |website=CNN |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2022/08/25/politics/biden-student-loan-relief-2022-midterms-analysis/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220907035322/https://edition.cnn.com/2022/08/25/politics/biden-student-loan-relief-2022-midterms-analysis/index.html |archive-date=September 7, 2022}} A majority of voters were found to support student loan forgiveness in the run-up to the election.{{Cite web |last=Guzman |first=Joseph |date=2022-08-24 |title=Most Americans support student loan forgiveness, poll finds |url=https://thehill.com/changing-america/enrichment/education/3614404-most-americans-support-student-loan-forgiveness-poll-finds/ |access-date=2022-11-01 |website=The Hill |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=October 14, 2022 |title=Harvard CAPS Harris Poll: October 12-13, 2022 |url=https://harvardharrispoll.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/HHP_Oct2022_KeyResults.pdf |publisher=Harvard Center for American Political Studies}} ====Presidency of Joe Biden==== Republicans are benefiting from President [[Joe Biden]]'s [[Opinion polling on the Joe Biden administration|low]] [[2022 opinion polling on the Joe Biden administration|approval ratings]], hovering from 30%-40% for much of the year. His ratings briefly increased after several legislative victories in August and September 2022,{{Cite news|website=Fox News|url=https://www.foxnews.com/politics/poll-democrats-midterm-chances-improve-inflation-abortion-remain-top-election-issues|title=Poll: Democrats' midterm chances improve while inflation and abortion remain top election issues|last=Spady|first=Aubrie|date=September 1, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220907061132/https://www.foxnews.com/politics/poll-democrats-midterm-chances-improve-inflation-abortion-remain-top-election-issues|archive-date=September 7, 2022}} but again plateaued in October when voters focused back on the state of the economy.{{Cite news|website=The Hill|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/3695528-biden-approval-rating-hovering-near-its-lowest-point-weeks-ahead-of-midterms-survey/|title=Biden approval rating hovering near its lowest point weeks ahead of midterms: survey|last=Gans|first=Jared|date=October 19, 2022}}{{Cite web |last=Cillizza |first=Chris |date=October 26, 2022 |title=Joe Biden’s poll numbers are in a very bad place for Democrats |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2022/10/26/politics/joe-biden-gallup-poll-midterm-elections/index.html |access-date=October 29, 2022 |website=[[CNN]]}} ====Russian invasion of Ukraine==== The [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]] is the major foreign policy issue, shifting support for Biden and highlighting the Republican party's perceived support for Russia.{{Cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/newsletter/2022-03-11/politics-war-ukraine-scrambles-plans-2022-midterm-election-essential-politics|title=Essential Politics: War in Ukraine scrambles GOP and Democratic strategies for midterms|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|last=Lauter|first=David|date=March 11, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220827125519/https://www.latimes.com/politics/newsletter/2022-03-11/politics-war-ukraine-scrambles-plans-2022-midterm-election-essential-politics|archive-date=August 27, 2022}}{{Cite news|website=CNN|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2022/03/27/politics/2022-midterm-elections-russia-ukraine-invasion/index.html|date=March 27, 2022|title=The 2022 campaign story was set. Then Russia invaded Ukraine.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220605005657/https://edition.cnn.com/2022/03/27/politics/2022-midterm-elections-russia-ukraine-invasion/index.html|archive-date=June 5, 2022|last1=Krieg|first1=Gregory|last2=Bradner|first2=Eric}} ==Federal elections== ===Senate elections=== {{main|2022 United States Senate elections}} Thirty-five of the 100 seats in the [[United States Senate|Senate]] will be up for election, including all 34 [[Classes of United States Senators#Class 3|Class 3]] seats. A special election is being held to fill a vacancy from another Senate class. As senators serve six-year terms, the last regularly scheduled elections for Class 3 senators were held in [[2016 United States Senate elections|2016]]. The winners of the United States Senate elections will be sworn in on January 3, 2023, for the [[118th United States Congress|118th Congress]]. ====Special elections==== Two special elections will take place in 2022 to replace senators who resigned during the [[117th United States Congress|117th Congress]]: *[[2022 United States Senate elections in California|California Class 3]]: Incumbent [[Kamala Harris]] was elected as [[Vice President of the United States]] and resigned on January 18, 2021, to take office also as the ''ex officio'' President of the Senate.{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/17/politics/kamala-harris-resigns-senate/index.html|title=Kamala Harris to resign Senate seat Monday|publisher=CNN|date=January 17, 2021|access-date=October 9, 2021|author=Wright, Jasmine}} [[Governor of California|Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] used his power to appoint the [[Secretary of State of California]], [[Alex Padilla]], to succeed her. A special election to fill the remaining weeks of Harris's tenure is to be held on November 8, 2022, the same day as the regular election for a six-year term, as a writ proclaimed by Newsom.{{cite web |last1=Newsom |first1=Gavin |title=Proclamation and Writ of Election |url=https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/Proclamation-and-Writ-of-Election-signed.pdf |publisher=Executive Department, State of California |access-date=October 9, 2021 |date=January 18, 2021}}{{Cite news|last=Wilson|first=Reid|date=September 28, 2021|title=California rule change means Padilla faces extra election|work=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]]|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/574242-california-rule-change-means-padilla-faces-extra-election|url-status=live|access-date=October 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210928225230/https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/574242-california-rule-change-means-padilla-faces-extra-election|archive-date=September 28, 2021}} *[[2022 United States Senate special election in Oklahoma|Oklahoma Class 2]]: Incumbent [[Jim Inhofe]] announced on February 24, 2022, that he will resign from the Senate at the end of the 117th Congress on January 3, 2023. A special election to fill the remaining four years of his term is to be held on November 8, 2022, concurrently with the [[2022 United States Senate election in Oklahoma|regular election]] for the Class 3 seat, held by [[James Lankford]].{{Cite news |last=Martin |first=Jonathan |date=February 24, 2022 |title=James Inhofe, Oklahoma Senator, Is Said to Plan an Early Retirement |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/24/us/politics/jim-inhofe-senate-retirement.html |access-date=February 24, 2022 |issn=0362-4331}} ===House of Representatives elections=== {{Main|2022 United States House of Representatives elections}} All 435 voting seats in the [[United States House of Representatives|House of Representatives]] will be up for election. Fifty-one representatives and one non-voting delegate (32 Democrats, 20 Republicans) have announced that they will be retiring or resigning early. The incumbents in these races were determined in the [[2020 United States House of Representatives elections|2020 House of Representatives elections]] and subsequent special elections. As these elections will be the first conducted after the post-[[2020 United States census|2020 census]] [[2020 United States redistricting cycle|redistricting]], several districts lack an incumbent or have multiple incumbents. ==== Special elections==== Eight special elections have already been held for the House of Representatives in 2022: *[[2022 Florida's 20th congressional district special election|Florida's 20th congressional district]]: [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick]] defeated Republican Jason Mariner to succeed Democrat [[Alcee Hastings]], who died on April 6, 2021, from [[pancreatic cancer]].{{Cite web|last=Homan|first=Timothy R.|date=April 6, 2021|title=Florida Rep. Alcee Hastings dead at 84|url=https://thehill.com/homenews/house/546638-florida-rep-alcee-hastings-dead-at-84|access-date=April 6, 2021|website=The Hill|language=en}}{{Cite web|last=Daugherty|first=Alex|title=DeSantis schedules special election for Alcee Hastings' seat in 2022|url=https://www.miamiherald.com/news/politics-government/article251160659.html|date=May 4, 2021|access-date=May 6, 2021|website=Miami Herald|language=en}}{{cite news |title=Democrat Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick wins House seat in Florida special election |first=David |last=Weigel |date=January 11, 2021 |access-date=January 11, 2021 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/house-election-florida/2022/01/10/22c9ea00-7278-11ec-b202-b9b92330d4fa_story.html |url-access=subscription}} The district has a partisan index of D+28. *[[2022 California's 22nd congressional district special election|California's 22nd congressional district]]: [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Connie Conway]] defeated Democrat Lourin Hubbard in a runoff to succeed Republican [[Devin Nunes]], who resigned on January 1, 2022, to become CEO of the [[Trump Media & Technology Group]].{{cite web|last=Korte|first=Lara|date=December 6, 2021|title=Devin Nunes' retirement could mean an opening for California Democrats. Who might run?|url=https://amp.sacbee.com/news/politics-government/capitol-alert/article256384562.html|access-date=December 6, 2021|website=Sacramento Bee}}{{cite news |title=Connie Conway is going to Washington D.C., wins Nunes' seat in Congress |orig-date=June 7, 2022 |date=June 8, 2022 |access-date=June 8, 2022 |work=Visalia Times Delta |url=https://www.visaliatimesdelta.com/story/news/2022/06/08/connie-conway-ahead-big-early-results-devin-nunes-seat-congress/7487017001/}} The district has a partisan index of R+6.{{Cite web |title=Introducing the 2021 Cook Political Report Partisan Voter Index |date=April 15, 2021 |last=Wasserman |first=David |url=https://cookpolitical.com/analysis/national/pvi/introducing-2021-cook-political-report-partisan-voter-index |access-date=April 16, 2021 |work=The Cook Political Report}} *[[2022 Texas's 34th congressional district special election|Texas's 34th congressional district]]: [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Mayra Flores]] defeated Democrat Dan Sanchez to succeed Democrat [[Filemon Vela Jr.]], who resigned on March 31, 2022, to work for [[Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld]].{{Cite news |last=Livingston |first=Abby |date=March 31, 2022 |title=U.S. Rep.
